title: Tensor formula for the right adjoint of a proper flat morphism
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $f:X\to S$ proper, flat and of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $a$ be a supplied right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], [def-pc-derived-direct-image], with counit $\epsilon$. For every $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(S)$ the canonical comparison
$$Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}a(\mathcal O_S)\longrightarrow a(M)$$
is an isomorphism [def-pc-derived-pullback], [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. The comparison is the $Rf_*\dashv a$ adjunct of the projection-formula composite $Rf_*(Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}a(\mathcal O_S))\simeq M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a(\mathcal O_S)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{\mathcal O_S}}M$. Thus the induced adjunction counit for the tensor functor is exactly this composite. No boundedness or Noetherian hypothesis is made.

proof.text: Put $R=Rf_*$, $L=Lf^*$, $\omega=a(\mathcal O_S)$ and $T(M)=LM\otimes^{\mathbf L}\omega$. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $f$. Thus $R$ preserves quasi-coherent cohomology, and pullback and tensor preserve it, so all these objects and functors lie in the indicated full subcategories. Choose the canonical strong monoidal pullback and its adjunction $L\dashv R$. The canonical projection map $M\otimes^{\mathbf L}R(E)\to R(LM\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)$ is, by its definition, the $L\dashv R$ transpose of the tensor comparison followed by the pullback counit; it is invertible by the projection formula. Write $p_{M,E}$ for its inverse. Define $\tau_M:T(M)\to a(M)$ by transposing $R(T(M))\xrightarrow{p_{M,\omega}}M\otimes^{\mathbf L}R\omega\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{\mathcal O_S}}M$. Naturality of the tensor comparison and both counits, and naturality of the adjunction bijection, give $a(u)\tau_M=\tau_N T(u)$ for every $u:M\to N$. Hence these are the components of a natural transformation $\tau:T\to a$.

proof.text: Let $K$ be perfect on $S$, with dual $K^\vee$. Perfect tensor-Hom duality, including its pullback compatibility, and the supplied adjunction $R\dashv a$ give, naturally in every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$, the bijections $$\operatorname{Hom}(E,TK)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(LK^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}E,\omega)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(R(LK^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}E),\mathcal O_S)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(K^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}RE,\mathcal O_S)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(RE,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(E,aK).$$ The middle bijection uses the canonical projection isomorphism. Apply the existing counit calculation [lem-sc-perfect-right-adjoint-tensor-hom-comparison] with $c=a$, its $K,D$ equal to $K,K^\vee$, and the two projection inverses pinned as in step 1: it says this composite sends each $q:E\to TK$ to $\tau_K\circ q$. Thus postcomposition with $\tau_K$ is bijective for every $E$. Surjectivity for $E=aK$ gives $s:aK\to TK$ with $\tau_Ks=1$; injectivity for $E=TK$ gives $s\tau_K=1$, by composing both candidate endomorphisms with $\tau_K$. Consequently $\tau_K$ is an isomorphism. No properness or Noetherian hypothesis is needed for this perfect-object calculation.

proof.text: The proper-flat direct-sum theorem applies to exactly the given qcqs base and proper, flat, finitely presented $f$, and to the supplied right adjoint $a$, so $a$ preserves all small direct sums. Both quasi-coherent derived categories have such sums. The adjunction $L\dashv R$ and preservation of colimits by left adjoints show that $L$ preserves them. Tensoring on the right by the fixed $\omega$ preserves ambient direct sums. Ambient sums exist and remain quasi-coherent, so they also compute sums in the full quasi-coherent subcategories (their universal property restricts to the same Hom sets). It follows that $T=(-\otimes^{\mathbf L}\omega)\circ L$ preserves these sums as well, including the empty sum.

proof.text: The separate-exact-structures theorem equips $T$ and $a$ with coherent exact integer-shift structures; its closure assumptions were verified in step 1, and it imposes no Noetherian condition. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-localizing-iso-locus] to the natural $\tau$ and these exact functors. Its coproduct hypotheses hold by step 3. Its perfect-shift hypothesis holds by step 2, because every integer shift of a perfect complex is perfect, as the same cited locus theorem states. Therefore $\tau_M$ is invertible on every shift of every $M$ in the perfect localizing closure. This uses the shift-saturated isomorphism locus and does not assume any unproved compatibility of $\tau$ with the independently chosen shifts.

source.place: Tag 0E4K, lemma-compare-with-pullback-flat-proper: localizing isomorphism locus, made precise by the existing shift-saturated locus theorem.

proof.text: By definition [def-pc-perfect-localizing-closure], the perfect localizing closure of $S$ is the smallest strictly full subcategory of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(S)$ containing every perfect complex and closed under shifts, cones, retracts and arbitrary set-indexed direct sums. Since $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, perfect localizing generation says that this subcategory is all of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(S)$. Taking shift zero in step 4 proves that the stated canonical comparison $\tau_M$ is an isomorphism for every unbounded quasi-coherent $M$.

source.place: Tag 0E4K, final generation argument; Tag 09IS, perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh.

proof.text: Write $b_M:R(T(M))\to M$ for the composite in step 1. The defining adjunction bijection gives $\epsilon_M\circ R(\tau_M)=b_M$. Transfer $R\dashv a$ along the natural isomorphism $\tau:T\xrightarrow{\sim}a$: the transferred Hom bijection sends $h:RE\to M$ to $\tau_M^{-1}\circ\operatorname{adj}(h)$. Its counit at $M$ is therefore $\epsilon_M\circ R(\tau_M)=b_M$. This proves the exact normalization of the induced counit, including the specified original counit rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of right adjoints.
